messages.content:
RoadDraft is a headless 2D CAD engine for roadway plans. Model space is US survey feet, and a point is [x, y] = [easting, northing] -- the other way round from how coordinates are usually spoken, so N 7300, E 4100 is [4100, 7300]. Sheets are paper inches seen through viewports at a feet-per-inch scale. Work through the commands: each one validates its params and explains what was wrong, every change is journaled and undoable. Start with get_document_state to see what is in the document, list_commands for the full surface, and render_sheet or render_model to look at your work.

To annotate something, find it before you point at it. In a sheet file the design usually lives in a referenced basefile, so the document owns no geometry of its own; find_entities searches the attachments too. Filter by what a thing IS -- layer, type, or its design anchor -- rather than dumping the document: find_entities {anchor: {kind: 'offset', offset: [-15, 15]}, visible_on: 'P-202'} is the pavement edges that sheet shows. Then pass the id straight to place_callout as target_entity, and the engine puts the leader tip on the geometry. Do not compute the point yourself: the midpoint of a curve's endpoints is not on the curve, and roadway linework runs parallel a few feet apart, so a hand-computed point usually lands on the wrong line rather than on nothing. If you do pass a raw target point, read the warning that comes back -- it names what the tip actually touched.

Some things are not entities at all -- a station, a PC, a point at an offset. Ask the design for those: list_alignments with include_references=true names a referenced alignment 'BASE:RTE-7', and station_to_xy, xy_to_station, resolve_anchor and get_design_data all accept that name and answer in host coordinates. To call one out, give place_callout a target_anchor ('86+50@15R', 'PC-2'; BC-2 and EC-2 name the PC and PT too) and that alignment name. Otherwise commands do not take it: nothing can be drawn, labelled or anchored to an alignment this document does not own.

Plan annotation belongs on the sheet, in paper inches, not in the model. Pass the sheet as place_callout's space and still name a model target -- target_entity or target_anchor: the engine sees it through the sheet's viewport (scale and twist included) and puts the tip where it shows on the paper. 'at' then runs along the part of the entity that sheet shows, since a pavement edge runs the whole project and a sheet shows one stretch. find_entities with visible_on gives each row a sheet_point, which is where that tip will land -- use it to choose a position for the text that is clear of the linework. Never work out a viewport by hand: model_to_sheet and sheet_to_model convert, and station_to_xy and point_on_entity take a sheet and answer in paper inches as well.

Drafting from a description works the same way: give the engine the description, not coordinates you worked out. A bearing and distance goes in as written -- create_alignment takes start + legs (each leg a bearing, azimuth or deflection and the distance to the next PI, with the radius of the curve at the PI it starts from), draw_traverse draws lines and curves course by course, and traverse computes the points without drawing. offset_entity copies linework parallel at a distance (one entity, or a chain offset as one path), fillet rounds the corner between two lines with a curve (a curb return), and measure with along gives distances along a line, chain or alignment and square off it. key_points and snap give the exact endpoints, intersections, centers and alignment design points (PI, BC, EC) to build on. Station-and-offset drafting is draw_station_offset with the stations and offsets given ('82+00@15R'). Linework drawn through something is cut back with trim (a point on the part to cut away) or run on with extend, not redrawn from computed points; break, join, lengthen, chamfer, copy, rotate, mirror, scale and array edit what is there. create_points sets COGO points, label_segments letters bearings and distances or L1/C1 tags with line and curve tables, place_along sets blocks or points at an interval, hatch fills an area (a point inside is enough), and area and get_entity read areas, lengths, bearings and curve data off the drawing.

Do one drafting task in a headless CAD engine called RoadDraft, using the tools you have been given. They are your ENTIRE tool surface.

Rules:
- Every change to the drawing must go through a tool call.
- The document is already open and saves itself after each command. Do not save it under another name.
- Nobody can answer questions. Work until you judge the task done, then stop and give your report.

THE TASK:
On sheet C-102, call out the edge of pavement. Draw the callout on the sheet itself, in paper space, the way plan annotation is drawn -- not in the model.

When finished, reply briefly with:
1. What you placed, in which space, and what it points at.
2. The tool calls that mattered, in order (tool name + the key arguments).
3. Anything that failed, confused you, or that you had to work around -- quote error messages.

Viewport center paper coordinates [17, 11.7], 1 inch = 50 feet. The main straight-line section is the T-2 tangent line segment. Good candidates:
- DESIGN:LN-005 (offset -12, left edge) — sheet_point [17.886, 12.0816], displayed 100%
- DESIGN:LN-008 (offset +12, right edge) — sheet_point [18.0377, 11.6263], displayed 100%

Call out one edge of the pavement — for example the right edge. Let's pick the left or right straight line, place the tip with target_entity at 'mid', and put the text on the sheet at a position that doesn't interfere with the linework.

The alignment runs roughly east (T-2, both line segments have the same length 1240.36, and the points are approximately [3369, 1269] and [3376, 1246] — the line runs slightly northeast/southeast). Paper sheet_point: left edge [17.886, 12.0816], right edge [18.0377, 11.6263]. So the left edge is above the right edge on paper (northing is larger = y is larger on paper).

Place the callout text to the right of the line (paper x is larger), e.g., position [22.5, 10.5]. Target the right edge LN-008, at 'mid' (midpoint of the visible portion). The leader tip lands at the sheet_point [18.0377, 11.6263].

Wait — the description of place_callout is as follows: "position: where the text is placed... when the target is on the left, the text starts here and extends to the right (left-aligned)." The target is to the left of the text position (the line is at x≈18, the text is at x≈22.5), so the text starts from here and extends to the right. The landing (the short horizontal segment) runs from the text back toward the target.

Text height on the sheet: the default when the sheet is specified is 0.10 inches. For the standard plan, 0.10–0.12 inches is fine. For the sheet annotation layer, the default is... there's no annotation layer in this document. The document's layers: 0, align_MAIN, rd_EP, rd_ES, rd_LAYOUT-NOTE-anno. The base file has rd_LAYOUT-NOTE-anno (layout note annotation). On the host document side, the same layer name exists — "rd_LAYOUT-NOTE-anno". It might be usable for annotations. The name suggests it's intended for annotation. But this is a host layer (layer list at the document level). The callout is drawn on the "current or specified layer." The current layer is "0". I think it's better to use "rd_LAYOUT-NOTE-anno" — this is clearly the annotation layer of this project.

Text content: "EDGE OF PAVEMENT" — classic callout. The task is "call out the edge of the pavement."

Callout: space C-102, target_entity DESIGN:LN-008, at mid, position [22.5, 10.5], content "EDGE OF PAVEMENT", height 0.10, layer rd_LAYOUT-NOTE-anno.

Which edge to target: LN-008 is the right side (offset +12). The line runs east; in CAD with x=easting, east is right. The right side of the travel direction = south side. On paper, the smaller y = below the line. Sheet point [18.0377, 11.6263] is below the left edge's [17.886, 12.0816].

If I put the text at [22.5, 10.5] (lower-right of the line), the target is to the left → the text is left-aligned starting from x=22.5. "EDGE OF PAVEMENT" is 16 characters, at 0.1 inch height the width is roughly 16 × 0.1 × 0.7 ≈ 1.12 inches. So it spans from 22.5 to about 23.6. The viewport extends to x=32.5 (center 17, width 31 → 1.5 to 32.5). No problem.

Landing is the default 2.5× the height = 0.25 inch, going back from the text position toward the target. The leader runs from the tip to the landing.

Hmm, but should the text be placed vertically centered on the target? No — the text is vertically centered on the position point. No problem.

As an alternative, place it above the left edge. There's the C-1 curve arc (AR-003/AR-005), sheet_point [3.8, 7.5], in the left-side region. Straight line + callout is cleaner.

I'll use the right edge LN-008. Actually, let me reconsider which is visually "the" edge of the pavement — either one is fine. I'll go with the right edge LN-008.

One consideration: 'at': 'mid' — "from the sheet, runs along the portion of the entity that the sheet displays, so mid is always a visible point to the reader." LN-008 is displayed 100%, so mid = the center of the entire line ≈ the midpoint of the visible portion. Good.

Alright, let's make the call.

**1. What I placed, where, and what it points at**

- A plan callout **"EDGE OF PAVEMENT"** (text height 0.10 in) on **sheet C-102, in paper space** (leader, landing, arrowhead and text are ordinary paper-inch entities there — nothing was drawn in model space).
- It points at **`DESIGN:LN-008`** — the referenced basefile's right edge of pavement: the straight tangent (T-2) at **12.00 ft right of alignment SR-100**, on layer `rd_EP`. The engine aimed the leader tip at the entity's mid point through viewport VP-002 (1"=50', no twist), landing at ≈ [18.04, 11.63] paper inches; the text sits at [22.5, 10.5] in the clear area below the road. Created: LN-001 (leader), LN-002 (landing), PL-001 (arrowhead), TX-001 (text), all on layer `rd_LAYOUT-NOTE-anno`.

**2. Tool calls that mattered, in order**

1. `get_document_state` + `list_sheets` — found sheet C-102 (SH-002) and that the document owns no model geometry of its own.
2. `list_references` — identified the design as attached reference **DESIGN** (`SR-100.model.rdoc.json`), with layers `align_MAIN`, `rd_EP`, `rd_ES`.
3. `get_sheet_state` (sheet C-102) — viewport VP-002: 1"=50', center [17, 11.7], no twist.
4. `find_entities` `{layer: "rd_EP", visible_on: "C-102", include_references: true}` — located the pavement edges actually shown on the sheet; picked `DESIGN:LN-008` (offset −12 = 12' RT, fully shown) and noted its `sheet_point` ≈ [18.04, 11.63] to place text clear of the linework.
5. `place_callout` `{space: "C-102", target_entity: "DESIGN:LN-008", at: "mid", position: [22.5, 10.5], content: "EDGE OF PAVEMENT", height: 0.1, layer: "rd_LAYOUT-NOTE-anno"}`.
6. `render_sheet` (C-102) — final check.

**3. Failures / confusion / workarounds**

- No errors, no warnings from any call.
- One judgment point, not a failure: `rd_EP` holds both pavement edges (±12' of SR-100). I called out the **right** edge (`LN-008`) as the representative "edge of pavement"; the left edge (`LN-005`) is a few inches below it on paper and a second callout there would crowd the road.
- The design geometry is read-only in a referenced basefile (`read_only: true`), which is why the callout is placed in sheet space via `target_entity` — the engine resolved the leader tip itself, so no hand-computed viewport arithmetic was needed.
